text.p: **** BIRTHDAYS ****
Danish philosopher SOREN KIERKEGAARD was born in 1813. He was one of the inventors of existentialism.

KARL MARX, the founder of Communism was born in 1818. The German scholar spent much of his life in London and Paris. His economic and political theories were first fully adopted by LENIN in Russia. He also lent his name to his followers, Marxists.
Australian Antarctic explorer SIR DOUGLAS MAWSON was born in 1882. He was the first geologist to reach the South Pole. He's has been honoured on the Australian 100 dollar note.

Australian prospector JOHN MILES was born in 1883. He was best known for finding silver and lead at Mt Isa in Queensland. He sold his leases there and spent the rest of his life wandering around the Australian bush.

American cinema heart throb TYRONE POWER was born in 1913. His films included "The Mark of Zorro" and "The Sun Also Rises". British comedian MICHAEL PALIN was born in 1943. PALIN first got into comedy acting at Cambridge University, and became one of the founding members of Monty Python. He later went solo with the comedy series "Ripping Yarns". One of his most popular roles was Pontius Pilot in "Life of Brian".
British bass player in the early days of 'Adam and the Ants' KEVIN PAUL MOONEY was born in 1962.
EVENTS

1821 : French Emperor NAPOLEON BONAPARTE died in exile on the island of St Helena. He had been imprisoned there by the British after the battle of Waterloo. He was hated at the time of his reign by the British and other Monarchies, but is still highly thought of in France. Debate has continued about whether
NAPOLEON was a monster or a saviour, but he has been universally accepted as the World's greatest general.
1865 : The world's first train robbery took place in Ohio.

1865 : Australian bush ranger BEN HALL dies after being shot 27 times by police in the Forbes district of New South Wales. His most famous escapade was holding up the entire town of Canowindra where he and his gang paid for the food and drink they consumed. HALL never killed anyone during his life of crime.

1926 : The first general strike in British history began after the Trades Union Congress voted to back the coal miners in their dispute with mine owners. The general strike continued for a week. The miners' strike continued for months with 250,000 miners returning to work in October 1926. The strike ended without resolution.
1945 : More than one-thousand Australian POWs had been repatriated from Europe to Britain.
1955 : The post-war occupation of Germany ended, with the creation of West Germany.
1968 : Paris was torn apart by riots involving students and police. The 30 thousand students were upset at the arrest of one of their leaders.
1968 : Three Australian journalists were killed by the Viet Cong in Saigon. A fourth escaped.

1980 : Watched by millions on television, The British Special Air Service or SAS stormed the Iranian embassy London and ended a six day siege. The terrorists had been demanding the release of prisoners in Iran. The SAS moved in and rescued 19 people, after the terrorists began killing hostages.
1988 : A Japanese television station broadcast the first transmission from the top of Mount Everest.
1989 : The number of reported AIDS cases world-wide had risen to more than 150,000. The virus was first reported in the early eighties.

1989 : In New Zealand, the Lange Government hit an all-time low recording a popularity of 30 percent. Three months later Prime Minister DAVID LANGE resigned after five years as leader of the Labor Party government. The reason for stepping-down from the top job was ill-health.

1989 : The former White House aide Lieutenant-Colonel OLIVER NORTH was found guilty on three counts arising from the Iran-Contra scandal. He was found NOT guilty on nine more serious charges. The 45-year-old Vietnam veteran was a key figure in the scheme to launder arms money from Iran and use it to support Contra rebels in Nicaragua. His defence was that he was merely following orders and that the plan had been devised by others. He was sentenced to two years probation and 1,200 hours of community service and fined 200-thousand dollars.
1994 : The English soccer club Arsenal won its first European Cup final in 24 years, defeating Italian team Parma 1-0.
